summary:
A streak is a run of consecutive day numbers, in any order in the input. Put the days in a hash set and only
count from days whose previous day is absent (streak starts); walk forward from each start. Every day is
visited a constant number of times: O(n).

question.md:
Return the length of the longest run of **consecutive day numbers** that all appear in `days`.

- **Order in the input doesn't matter:** `[100, 4, 200, 1, 3, 2]` contains 1, 2, 3, 4: length 4.
- **Repeats don't extend a streak:** practising twice on day 5 is still one day.
- **Empty input** gives 0.
- **Day numbers are ±10⁹**, so they can't index an array.
- The same idea as **Longest Chain With a Step** with step 1.

think.md: Take `[100, 4, 200, 1, 3, 2, 101, 102, 50]`. The streaks are 1-2-3-4 (length 4), 100-101-102 (length 3), and single days 200 and 50.

think.caption: Shaded: each streak's first day, the only day whose previous day is missing.

think.md:
Two natural tools: **sorting** puts each streak's days side by side; a **hash set** answers "is day d + 1
present?" in O(1). With the set, the trick is to start counting only at a streak's first day (where d − 1 is
absent). Starting anywhere else would re-walk part of a streak already counted.

approaches.title: Extend from every day by scanning

idea.md: For each day d, look for d + 1 in the list, then d + 2, and so on, each time with a full scan. Keep the longest streak found.

build: While `d + length` appears in the list (scan), `length += 1`.
Keep the maximum (0 for an empty list).

lines.text: Linear search for a day number (64-bit, since `d + length` can pass 2³¹ − 1 near 10⁹).
Every day gets a turn as a streak start.
Longest streak; 0 when there are no days.

complexity.md: **Time O(n³)** in the worst case (a streak of n days, re-walked from each day, each step scanning n). **Space O(1).**

walk.title: From every day, extend the streak forward by scanning the list for the next day.

limits.md: Scanning answers membership slowly, and every day re-walks its streak. Sorting fixes both at once.

approaches.title: Sort, then scan

idea.md: Sort a copy. Walk it: an equal neighbour is a repeat (ignore); a neighbour exactly one larger extends the current streak; anything else starts a new streak of 1.

build: If there are no days, return 0.
For each i ≥ 1: equal → skip; +1 → `current += 1`; otherwise `current = 1`. Update `best`.

lines.text: Sorted copy: each streak's days become neighbours.
The first day alone is a streak of 1.
Same day again: doesn't extend or break the streak.
Exactly one more than the previous day extends the streak; any bigger jump starts over. `s[i − 1] + 1` stays within `int` because days are ≤ 10⁹.

complexity.md: **Time O(n log n).** **Space O(n)** for the copy.

walk.title: Sort; walk through, extending the current streak on +1, ignoring repeats, restarting otherwise.

limits.md: The sort orders all days, but each streak only needs "is d + 1 present?", which a hash set answers in O(1).

approaches.title: Hash set, counting from streak starts

idea.md: Put all days in a hash set. For each distinct day d whose previous day d − 1 is **not** present, walk forward d + 1, d + 2, … while present, and record the length. Each streak is walked once, from its start.

build: Build a hash set of the days.
For each distinct d: skip if d − 1 is in the set.
Otherwise walk forward while the next day is present; keep the longest length.

lines.text: C has no hash set, so these few lines build one. `slotOf` scrambles a key into a starting slot (multiply by a large odd constant, keep the well-mixed high bits). `has` walks forward from there until it finds the key or an empty slot; `add` walks the same way and claims the slot. With the table at most half full, each call is O(1) on average.
All distinct days in a hash set.

notes.cpp: `long long` keys, so `d ± 1` near ±10⁹ can't overflow.
notes.c: A table at least twice the number of days; repeats collapse into one entry.
Walk the table's used slots: exactly the distinct days.

lines.text: If the previous day is present, this day is in the middle of a streak that its first day will measure.
A streak start: count forward while the next day exists.
Longest streak; 0 for an empty list.

complexity.md: **Time O(n)** on average: each day is checked as a possible start once and walked over at most once. **Space O(n)** for the set.

walk.title: Put the days in a hash set; only start counting at days whose previous day is missing.

takeaways.md:
- Longest run of consecutive values: hash set + **start only where the previous value is missing**.
- Sorting and scanning is the hash-free alternative (O(n log n)); remember to skip repeats.
- Same pattern as **Longest Chain With a Step**: replace +1 with +step.
